title: Rule fields beyond criteria: reauth, posture notification and profile IDs

prose.text: Some rule fields sit outside the criteria, and their behavior is mostly set by the clients.

prose.label: Reauthentication fields.
prose.text: {{reauth-fields-none}} What an unset value means is open {{gap:reauth-unset-meaning}}. {{reauth-force-new-v1}} {{v2-timeout-not-force-new}} Whether the API refuses an in-place change is open {{gap:reauth-update-refused-by-api}}.

prose.label: Profile references.
prose.text: {{profile-id-fields}} {{isolation-profile-required-for-isolate}} What happens with a mismatched profile ID is open {{gap:irrelevant-profile-id-effect}}.
The credential references on PRA rules are in [[zpa.terraform.policy-rule-writes]]. Timeout values are in [[zpa.policy.timeout-rules]].

checks.do: Before changing a timeout on an existing v1 Terraform rule, check whether the resource uses the shared schema that forces a new resource.
For a posture block users do not see explained, check the rule's device posture failure notification flag and the client version.
For an isolation or inspection rule, check that the profile ID matches the rule's action.

reauth-fields-none.statement: The Python rule model reads `reauth_timeout` and `reauth_idle_timeout` as None when the rule does not carry them.

quotes: self.reauth_idle_timeout = config["reauthIdleTimeout"] if "reauthIdleTimeout" in config else None
self.reauth_timeout = config["reauthTimeout"] if "reauthTimeout" in config else None

reauth-force-new-v1.statement: In the shared policy schema of the Terraform provider, used by the forwarding, access, timeout and redirection rule resources, `reauth_timeout` and `reauth_idle_timeout` are ForceNew, so changing either on an existing rule plans a destroy and recreate.

quotes: "reauth_idle_timeout": { Type: schema.TypeString, Optional: true, ForceNew: true, },
"reauth_timeout": { Type: schema.TypeString, Optional: true, ForceNew: true, },

v2-timeout-not-force-new.statement: The v2 timeout rule resource declares `reauth_timeout` and `reauth_idle_timeout` without ForceNew. From v4.4.15 both carry the `DiffSuppressFunc` `suppressEquivalentTimeout`, which hides a difference between two timeouts of the same duration (for example `Never` and `never`, or `60 Minutes` and `1 Hour`); up to v4.4.14 they had no diff suppression.

quotes: "reauth_idle_timeout": { Type: schema.TypeString, Optional: true, DiffSuppressFunc: suppressEquivalentTimeout, },
"reauth_timeout": { Type: schema.TypeString, Optional: true, DiffSuppressFunc: suppressEquivalentTimeout, },
// suppressEquivalentTimeout ignores differences between timeouts of the same
// duration, e.g. "Never" and "never", or "60 Minutes" and the "1 Hour" read back.
`zpa_policy_timeout_rule_v2`: equivalent timeouts (such as `Never` and `never`, or `60 Minutes` and `1 Hour`) no longer show as a change in every plan.

device-posture-notification.statement: A rule's device posture failure notification flag is the JSON key `devicePostureFailureNotificationEnabled`, and the message it enables displays only for Client Connector 4.8 or later on Windows and 5.0 or later on macOS, with a notification template that enables it.

quotes: The message displays only if the associated access policy has the Device Posture Failure Notification enabled and the user's app profile includes a notification template with Show Device Posture Failure Remediation Notification enabled.
Applies only to Zscaler Client Connector version 4.8 and later for Windows and Zscaler Client Connector version 5.0 and later for macOS.

isolation-profile-required-for-isolate.statement: The Python `add_isolation_rule` requires `zpn_isolation_profile_id` when the action is isolate and checks nothing about the profile ID for other actions.

evidence.after: def add_isolation_rule(self, name: str, action: str, zpn_isolation_profile_id: str = None, **kwargs)

profile-id-fields.statement: Rules carry the profile references as `zpnIsolationProfileId`, `zpnInspectionProfileId` and `zpnInspectionProfileName`.

reauth-unset-meaning.title: What an unset reauth_timeout or reauth_idle_timeout on a rule means
reauth-unset-meaning.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Both default to `None`, meaning the global tenant setting applies when a rule doesn't override. If a user asks 'why is this session re-auth-ing sooner than the rule says', check both the rule value and the tenant global." The model default is documented (claim reauth-fields-none); the help describes a default timeout rule rather than a tenant global setting. See divergence timeout-defaults in zpa.policy.timeout-rules.

reauth-update-refused-by-api.title: Whether the ZPA API itself refuses to change reauth timeouts in place
reauth-update-refused-by-api.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "Both are `ForceNew` at the Terraform/API level ... the API refuses in-place updates ... the rule is deleted and re-created, which can shuffle rule order and cause transient policy gaps." ForceNew is a Terraform schema property (claim reauth-force-new-v1) and the v2 timeout resource does not set it (claim v2-timeout-not-force-new), so the provider alone does not show an API refusal. Where a recreated rule lands in the order is covered in zpa.terraform.rule-order. Send a PUT that changes only the timeout in a scratch tenant.

irrelevant-profile-id-effect.title: What the API does with a profile ID that does not match the rule's action
irrelevant-profile-id-effect.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the isolation profile is "only relevant when `action = ISOLATE`", the inspection profile "only relevant when `action = INSPECT`", the SDK does not validate that, and "the API's behavior in that case is unstated." The Python helper validates presence for isolate only (claim isolation-profile-required-for-isolate); no captured source says the profile is ignored for other actions. Send a mismatched profile ID in a scratch tenant.
